pattern.crimePattern: a banker who finds his wife's secret phone uses it to lure her lover to his studio gym and kills him, while his driver waits in the lane and later swears he never left home
pattern.notes: Fictional people, studio and compound. Twist: the lure came from the wife's second phone, but she never sent it. Accomplice: the driver, who knowingly drove and lied. Honest staff witness: the compound caretaker.

ob.text: A cleaner reports a personal trainer found dead on the floor of his private studio gym in a Kileleshwa apartment compound: Andrew Simiyu (38).

facts.text: Andrew Simiyu, a personal trainer, was found dead in his studio gym in Kileleshwa on Wednesday morning.
One crushing blow to the side of Andrew's head.
A 16 kg kettlebell is back on the rack with its handle wiped; every other handle carries chalk handprints.
KSh 30,000 of equipment and Andrew's phone were left behind.
Andrew's phone, Tuesday 20:12, from "N.": "Can you open the studio at 9? I need to see you. Side door." He replied, "On my way."
The booking app: Felix and Nyokabi Onyango are both Andrew's clients.
A year of client reviews and not one complaint.
The studio accounts: a KSh 900,000 loan to Ian Waweru, Andrew's former partner, unpaid.
Mama Grace: a dark Mercedes stopped in the back lane at about ten to nine, lights off. A tall man in a cap went in the side door and came out fast about 25 minutes later. The driver never got out.
Mama Grace was in her gatehouse with her grandchildren all evening.
Mama Grace: Andrew opens the side door himself; only he has the key.
Records ①: "N." is a second line registered to Nyokabi Onyango.
Records ①: at 20:12 the "N." phone was on the Lavington mast, at the Onyango house, not in Westlands.
Six months of "N." messages, and a Naivasha hotel booking for "Mr & Mrs Simiyu" on a weekend Felix was in London.
The café host and booking: Nyokabi was at the book club 19:30–22:15 with eleven women; her main phone was on the Westlands mast all evening.
Records ②: Felix's Mercedes left the Lavington house at 20:40, stood in the lane behind the studio 20:52–21:20, and was home at 21:33.
Josphat's first statement: "I drove Bwana home from the office at seven. He never left. I washed the car and slept in my quarters."
In Nyokabi's drawer: the second phone, switched off. Last used: Tuesday 20:14.
In Felix's car: a dark cap on the back seat, chalk dust on the rear mat, and small dark spots under it.
Purity: Felix left the office at 18:40 on Tuesday, not 19:00, and said he had "a private matter".
Ian has been in Mombasa since Monday: flight and hotel.
Josphat sat in the car in the lane, engine off, 20:52–21:20.
Fingerprints taken from Felix in detention.
Post-mortem: one blow from a heavy, rounded iron object, matching a kettlebell.
Post-mortem: death on Tuesday between 20:50 and 21:30.
Lab: Felix's thumb on the back of the second phone, over Nyokabi's older prints.
Lab: the chalk on the car mat is the studio's gym chalk, with its added scent.
Lab: the spots under the chalk on the car mat are Andrew's blood.

reconstruction.text: Nyokabi has been seeing Andrew for six months on a second phone she keeps in her dressing-table drawer. On Sunday Felix finds it and reads it all. He says nothing.
Tuesday. Nyokabi goes to her book club in Westlands with her main phone. At 20:12 Felix texts Andrew from the second phone: "Can you open the studio at 9? Side door." Andrew: "On my way."
At 20:40 Josphat drives Felix to the lane behind the studio and waits, lights off. Felix goes in the side door. He strikes Andrew with a 16 kg kettlebell, wipes the handle and puts it back.
At 21:20 the car leaves; at 21:33 Felix is home. He switches the second phone off and puts it back in the drawer. In the morning he tells Josphat: "You drove me home at seven." Josphat says it.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on the "N." line, then the car's fleet tracker. No warrant: Nyokabi opens her drawer and Felix lets you look in the car. Detain Felix after the tracker; prints (6 h) come back well inside 24 h; the chalk and blood traces (12 h) go as soon as the car mat is bagged.
